question: Find: $\int\frac{\cos x}{\sin 3x}dx$
explanation:
**Step 1:** Use $\sin 3x=\sin x(3-4\sin^2x)$. Then
$$\int\frac{\cos x}{\sin x(3-4\sin^2x)}dx.$$

**Step 2:** Put $t=\sin x$, so $dt=\cos x\,dx$. Then
$$\int\frac{dt}{t(3-4t^2)}.$$ Using partial fractions,
$$\frac{1}{t(3-4t^2)}=\frac{1}{3t}+\frac{4t}{3(3-4t^2)}.$$

**Step 3:** Integrating,
$$\frac{1}{3}\log|t|-\frac{1}{6}\log|3-4t^2|+C.$$

Substituting $t=\sin x$,
$$\frac{1}{3}\log|\sin x|-\frac{1}{6}\log|3-4\sin^2x|+C.$$
